from: GENERAL NORMS LIBER I. DE NORMIS GENERALIBUS
reason: On the one page where Book I actually opens, the EN edition prints the Latin edition's own book title run into the English one inside a single <b> -- 'GENERAL NORMS LIBER I. DE NORMIS GENERALIBUS' -- with no separator of any kind between them. There is no markup to read, so no parser can divide them; the whole string becomes the book's title and stands at the head of every breadcrumb in Book I. The Latin half is not a translation the EN edition offers (it offers none anywhere else, in any book), it is the Latin edition's heading left in.
evidence:
raw/cic/en/cic_lib1-cann1-6_en.html: '

BOOK I.

GENERAL NORMS LIBER I. DE NORMIS GENERALIBUS

'. The same edition prints the title as 'BOOK I. GENERAL NORMS' on the breadcrumb line of twelve other pages of Book I (cic_lib1-cann7-22_en.html, ...cann23-28, ...cann29-34, ...cann94-95, ...cann96-123, ...cann124-128, ...cann129-144, ...cann145-196, ...cann197-199, ...cann200-203, among others) -- so the correct reading is witnessed repeatedly inside this edition and nothing is imported from another. Compare cic_lib4-cann834-848_en.html, where the same two lines are printed as SEPARATE paragraphs ('FUNCTION OF THE CHURCH' then 'LIBER IV. DE ECCLESIAE MUNERE SANCTIFICANDI'), which is what makes the Book I paragraph a transcription slip rather than the edition's convention.
